text: By the residue theorem, the contour integral ∮_C f(z) dz of a function meromorphic on and inside a simple closed contour C equals:
choices: the sum of the residues at the poles inside C
2πi times the sum of the residues at the poles inside C
2πi times the value f(z₀) at the centre of C
explanation: The residue theorem states ∮_C f dz = 2πi Σ Res_{z=z_k} f, summed over poles inside C. Dropping the 2πi factor is a common slip; the integral is 0 only when f is holomorphic (no interior poles) by Cauchy's theorem; and 2πi·f(z₀) belongs to the Cauchy integral formula for f(z)/(z − z₀).
